title: Beechcraft Baron 58 — Normal Operating Procedures
description: Normal operating procedures for the Beechcraft Baron 58 with twin Continental IO-550 fuel-injected engines, constant-speed propellers, and retractable tricycle gear. Covers preflight walk-around through shutdown and securing. Each engine has its own fuel selector (LEFT / RIGHT / OFF) — verify the correct tank is selected for each engine before each phase. The IO-550 is fuel-injected; there is no carburetor heat. Counter-rotating propellers on the Baron cancel most P-factor at cruise power, but VMC and single-engine handling characteristics require type-specific training. All airspeeds, power settings, fuel quantities, manifold pressure values, and performance data must come from the specific aircraft POH. Not a substitute for qualified twin-engine instruction or Baron-specific checkout.

source.notes: No manufacturer document consulted. Written from general familiarity with the type.

known_issues.description: Contains no airspeeds, power settings, fuel quantities, or other numerical limitations — all must come from the specific aircraft POH.
Equipment variations exist across Baron 58 airframes. Verify every item against the specific aircraft and its POH before use.

rights.notes: Manufacturer POH remains under copyright. This file does not reproduce its wording or selection of items.
